   - Added cleanup code to destroy the `preempt_fence_wq` in the `xe_device_destroy` function.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications establish a new device-specific work queue for handling preempt fences, which is crucial for preventing starvation of the global `system_unbound_wq`. The addition of the `preempt_fence_wq` in the `xe_device` structure allows for better management of preempt fence operations, ensuring that they can wait without affecting other system operations. The allocation and destruction of this work queue are handled in the device creation and destruction functions, respectively, ensuring proper resource management and cleanup. Overall, these changes enhance the efficiency and reliability of the preempt fence handling in the DRM driver for Intel GPUs.

Here is the commit message:
drm/xe: Use ordered wq for preempt fence waiting

Preempt fences can sleep waiting for an exec queue suspend operation to
complete. If the system_unbound_wq is used for waiting and the number of
waiters exceeds max_active this will result in other users of the
system_unbound_wq getting starved. Use a device private work queue for
preempt fences to avoid starvation of the system_unbound_wq.

Even though suspend operations can complete out-of-order, all suspend
operations within a VM need to complete before the preempt rebind worker
can start. With that, use a device private ordered wq for preempt fence
waiting.

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug is that preempt fences were using the `system_unbound_wq` for waiting, which could lead to starvation of other users of this work queue when the number of waiters exceeded the maximum active limit. This situation could cause delays in processing other tasks, as the preempt fence waiters could monopolize the work queue, leading to performance degradation and potential deadlocks in the system.

Here is the patch:
 
 static bool preempt_fence_enable_signaling(struct dma_fence *fence)
 {
 	struct xe_preempt_fence *pfence =
 		container_of(fence, typeof(*pfence), base);
 	struct xe_exec_queue *q = pfence->q;
 
 	pfence->error = q->ops->suspend(q);
-	queue_work(system_unbound_wq, &pfence->preempt_work);
+	queue_work(q->vm->xe->preempt_fence_wq, &pfence->preempt_work);
 	return true;
 }
